samples.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row; count them 1 to 5 from left to right. Each panel contains five upright pillars of the same width, standing on the same invisible floor line at the bottom of that panel, spaced evenly across the panel, so a pillar is taller exactly when its top edge stands higher above that common floor. All five panels carry exactly the same five pillar heights and exactly the same five pillar fill shades; only the left-to-right arrangement of those pillars differs from panel to panel. Because of this, the number of pillars, the total amount of ink, the tallest height, the shortest height and the set of shades are identical in every panel and carry no information. The fill shade of a pillar is decoration only: two of the five panels happen to have their shades running steadily from dark to light or from light to dark across the panel, and that shading has nothing to do with the answer, which depends on pillar height alone. In exactly one panel the pillars get taller at every step from left to right, so each pillar is taller than the pillar immediately to its left. In each of the other four panels that run is broken at least once: somewhere in the row a pillar is shorter than the pillar immediately to its left, and every such drop, as well as every rise in the ascending panel, is at least seventeen pixels, so no comparison is a close call. Which numbered panel has its five pillars increasing in height at every step from left to right? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
